app.name: ReviveGuard
summary.hint_fix: Run 'reviveguard fix' to review available remediation.
summary.not_root: Not running as root: some checks use fallback methods and may be less accurate.
summary.unsupported_os: This operating system is not in the tested support list.
ssh.root_login.title: SSH root login
ssh.root_login.desc: Direct root login over SSH increases the impact of password guessing and credential theft.
ssh.root_login.fix: Set 'PermitRootLogin no' (or 'prohibit-password') after confirming another administrator account with working access exists.
ssh.password_auth.title: SSH password authentication
ssh.password_auth.desc: Password logins can be brute-forced; key-based authentication is much harder to attack.
ssh.password_auth.fix: Set 'PasswordAuthentication no' only after verifying key-based login works for an administrator account.
ssh.empty_passwords.title: SSH empty passwords
ssh.empty_passwords.desc: Accounts with empty passwords must never be able to log in over SSH.
ssh.pubkey_auth.title: SSH public key authentication
ssh.pubkey_auth.desc: Public key authentication is the recommended login method; if disabled, only weaker methods remain.
ssh.config_perms.title: SSH daemon configuration permissions
ssh.config_perms.desc: sshd_config must be owned by root and not writable by group or others.
ssh.skipped: SSH server is not installed or its configuration cannot be read.
ssh.module.title: SSH configuration
scanner.check_error: The check could not be completed due to an internal error.
rollback.warn_modified: WARNING: {path} was modified after the fix; its current content will be overwritten.
rollback.err.already: this operation was already rolled back.
rollback.err.not_reversible: this operation cannot be reliably reversed (for example a package upgrade).
fix.backup_note: A backup is created first; undo later with 'reviveguard rollback'.
fix.prompt_disruptive: This change can affect remote access. Keep a second SSH session open. Type 'yes' to continue:
fix.result.applied: Applied and verified ({id}). Undo with: reviveguard rollback --id {id}
fix.result.apply_failed: Applying the change failed ({detail}); the change was reverted.
fix.result.validation_failed: Configuration validation failed ({detail}); the change was reverted.
fix.result.activation_failed: The service did not accept the change ({detail}); the change was reverted.
fix.result.verify_failed: Verification failed ({detail}); the change was reverted.
fix.result.revert_failed: URGENT: automatic restore failed. Run 'reviveguard rollback --id {id}' or restore the backup manually.
fix.err.not_root: Fixes must be run as root.
fix.err.unsupported_os: Fixes are only enabled on tested systems (Debian 12+, Ubuntu 22.04+).
fix.err.disabled: Remediation is disabled in the configuration.
fix.service.reload_ssh: The SSH service will be reloaded (not restarted); existing sessions stay connected.
fix.ssh.chmod: set owner root:root and mode 0600 on {path}
fix.reason.no_autofix: no safe automatic fix exists for this finding.
fix.reason.no_sshd: the SSH server or its validator (sshd -t) is not available.
fix.reason.config_invalid: the current SSH configuration is already invalid (sshd -t fails); fix that first.
fix.reason.no_include: sshd_config does not include /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf, so a safe drop-in cannot be used.
fix.reason.directive_before_include: '{key}' is set in sshd_config before the Include line, so a drop-in would be ignored; edit it manually.
fix.reason.cannot_determine_user: this is a remote session but the login user could not be determined.
fix.reason.no_key_for_current_user: user '{user}' (the current login) has no verified working access that would survive this change.
fix.reason.root_session_no_key: you are logged in remotely as root and root has no valid authorized_keys; changing this could lock you out.
fix.reason.no_admin_access: no administrator account with verified key (or password) access exists; changing this could lock everyone out.
fix.reason.pubkey_disabled: public key authentication is disabled, so password login is the only method.
fix.reason.auth_methods: AuthenticationMethods is customized; disabling passwords may break the required method chain.
firewall.module.title: Firewall
firewall.needs_root: Firewall rules can only be read as root; run the audit with sudo.
firewall.unreadable: Firewall tools are installed but their rules could not be read.
firewall.policy_unknown: The default incoming policy could not be determined for the firewall in use.
firewall.active.title: Firewall active
firewall.active.desc: Without an active firewall every listening service is reachable from the network.
firewall.active.fix: Allow your SSH port first (e.g. 'ufw allow <ssh-port>/tcp'), review other required ports, then enable the firewall ('ufw enable'). Keep a second SSH session open. ReviveGuard does not enable firewalls automatically.
firewall.default_policy.title: Firewall default incoming policy
firewall.default_policy.desc: A firewall that accepts incoming traffic by default only blocks what was listed explicitly.
firewall.default_policy.fix: Set the default incoming policy to deny only after every required port is allowed (e.g. 'ufw default deny incoming').
firewall.dangerous_rules.title: Dangerous firewall rules
firewall.dangerous_rules.desc: Rules that expose database or admin ports to everyone, or accept all traffic, defeat the firewall.
firewall.dangerous_rules.fix: Restrict the listed rules to trusted addresses or remove them after confirming nothing depends on them.
firewall.conflict.title: Conflicting firewall managers
firewall.conflict.desc: UFW and firewalld both manage rules and can overwrite each other's configuration.
firewall.conflict.fix: Use one firewall manager: disable the one you do not need, after copying its required rules.
fail2ban.module.title: Fail2ban
fail2ban.needs_root: Fail2ban state can only be read as root; run the audit with sudo.
fail2ban.unreadable: Fail2ban is running but its status could not be read.
fail2ban.running.title: Fail2ban running
fail2ban.running.desc: Fail2ban bans addresses with repeated failed logins and slows down brute-force attacks.
fail2ban.running.fix: Install and enable it ('apt install fail2ban', 'systemctl enable --now fail2ban'). ReviveGuard can install it (with your confirmation).
fail2ban.config_valid.title: Fail2ban configuration valid
fail2ban.config_valid.desc: An invalid configuration can prevent jails from loading after the next restart.
fail2ban.config_valid.fix: Run 'fail2ban-client -t', fix the reported error, then reload fail2ban.
fail2ban.ssh_jail.title: Fail2ban SSH jail
fail2ban.ssh_jail.desc: Without the sshd jail, repeated SSH login failures are never banned.
fail2ban.ssh_jail.fix: Enable the sshd jail (ReviveGuard can do this through a drop-in in /etc/fail2ban/jail.d/).
fail2ban.log_backend.title: Fail2ban log source
fail2ban.log_backend.desc: If the jail cannot read SSH logs it will never see failures, so nothing is banned.
fail2ban.log_backend.fix: Use backend=systemd on journald systems, or point logpath at an existing auth log.
fail2ban.ban_settings.title: Fail2ban ban settings
fail2ban.ban_settings.desc: Very short bans or a high retry limit make brute force cheap for attackers.
fail2ban.ban_settings.fix: Use e.g. bantime = 1h and maxretry = 5 in a jail.d drop-in; add your own address to ignoreip to avoid banning yourself.
fix.fail2ban.enable_jail: create {path} enabling the sshd jail on port {port}
fix.service.reload_fail2ban: Fail2ban will be reloaded (not restarted). Repeated failed logins from your own address can get it banned; consider adding it to ignoreip.
fix.reason.firewall_manual: firewall changes are never applied automatically; follow the recommendation below with a second SSH session open.
fix.reason.fail2ban_config_invalid: the current fail2ban configuration is invalid ('fail2ban-client -t' fails); fix that first.
fix.reason.no_fail2ban_dir: /etc/fail2ban/jail.d does not exist, so a safe drop-in cannot be used.
updates.module.title: System updates
updates.no_apt: apt is not available; update checks are skipped.
updates.index_stale: The package index is stale, so available updates cannot be judged. Refresh it first (UPD-001).
updates.unreadable: The list of upgradable packages could not be read.
updates.index_fresh.title: Package index freshness
updates.index_fresh.desc: With an old or missing package index the system cannot see available security updates.
updates.security_updates.title: Security updates
updates.security_updates.desc: Security updates fix known vulnerabilities; unpatched packages are a common way into servers.
updates.security_updates.fix: Install them ('apt-get install --only-upgrade <package>') or let ReviveGuard apply only the security ones.
updates.reboot.title: Reboot after updates
updates.reboot.desc: A reboot is pending, so some updates (for example a new kernel) are not active yet.
updates.reboot.fix: Reboot at a convenient time ('reboot'). ReviveGuard never reboots the server.
updates.auto_updates.title: Automatic security updates
updates.auto_updates.desc: Without automatic security updates the server stays vulnerable until someone logs in.
updates.auto_updates.fix: Install unattended-upgrades and enable it (ReviveGuard can do this).
updates.os_supported.title: Operating system support
updates.os_supported.desc: This OS is outside ReviveGuard's supported list (Debian 12+, Ubuntu 22.04+) and may no longer get security updates.
fix.updates.index: run 'apt-get update' to refresh the package index
fix.updates.security: upgrade {count} package(s) from the security pocket only: {packages}
fix.firewall.install_ufw: install the ufw package (it stays disabled; no firewall rules are changed)
fix.fail2ban.install: set up fail2ban (packages: {packages}), enable the sshd jail with a log source and ban mechanism that exist on this host, and whitelist your SSH address ({ip})
fix.service.packages_may_restart: Upgrades can restart services (for example ssh); existing sessions normally survive. A reboot may be needed afterwards.
fix.not_reversible_note: Package changes cannot be undone by 'reviveguard rollback'; the operation is only recorded in the history.
fix.result.not_reversible: Package changes are not rolled back automatically ({id}). Check the state with 'dpkg --audit' and 'apt-get -f install' if needed.
fix.rerun_hint: Run 'reviveguard audit' again: some fixes reveal follow-up findings.
fix.reason.no_apt: apt is not available on this system.
fix.reason.nothing_to_upgrade: no security updates are currently listed; refresh the package index first.
fix.reason.fail2ban_inactive: fail2ban is installed but not running; start it with 'systemctl enable --now fail2ban'.
fix.reason.reboot_manual: ReviveGuard never reboots a server; reboot it yourself when convenient.
fix.reason.os_manual: upgrading the operating system release is a manual task.
permissions.accounts.title: Account files permissions
permissions.accounts.desc: /etc/passwd and /etc/group must be owned by root and not writable by others.
permissions.accounts.fix: chown root:root and chmod 644 the listed files (ReviveGuard can tighten them).
permissions.shadow.title: Password hash files permissions
permissions.shadow.desc: /etc/shadow and /etc/gshadow hold password hashes; readable by others they enable offline cracking.
permissions.shadow.fix: chmod 640 (or 600) and chown root the listed files (ReviveGuard can tighten them).
permissions.sudoers.title: Sudoers files permissions
permissions.sudoers.desc: Writable or world-readable sudoers files allow privilege escalation or leak policy.
permissions.sudoers.fix: chown root and chmod 440 the listed files (ReviveGuard can tighten them).
permissions.host_keys.title: SSH host private keys permissions
permissions.host_keys.desc: Readable host private keys let others impersonate the server.
permissions.host_keys.fix: chown root:root and chmod 600 the listed keys (ReviveGuard can tighten them).
sysctl.ip_forward.title: IP forwarding
sysctl.ip_forward.desc: Packet forwarding turns the host into a router; it is only needed for routers, VPN and Docker hosts.
sysctl.ip_forward.fix: Set net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0 if this host is not a router (ReviveGuard does not change it automatically).
sysctl.accept_redirects.title: ICMP redirect handling
sysctl.accept_redirects.desc: Accepting ICMP redirects lets a neighbour alter this host's routing.
sysctl.source_route.title: Source routing handling
sysctl.source_route.desc: Source-routed packets let an attacker choose the packet path and bypass filters.
sysctl.syncookies.title: TCP SYN cookies
sysctl.syncookies.desc: SYN cookies protect against SYN-flood denial of service.
sysctl.kptr_restrict.title: Kernel pointer exposure
sysctl.kptr_restrict.desc: Exposed kernel addresses make kernel exploits easier.
sysctl.dmesg_restrict.title: Kernel log access
sysctl.dmesg_restrict.desc: Unprivileged access to dmesg can leak kernel information.
sysctl.aslr.title: Address space randomization (ASLR)
sysctl.aslr.desc: Without full ASLR memory-corruption exploits are far more reliable.
sysctl.rp_filter.title: Reverse path filtering
sysctl.rp_filter.desc: Reverse path filtering drops spoofed-source packets.
sysctl.rp_filter.fix: Set net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter = 1 (or 2), unless asymmetric routing or a VPN needs otherwise (manual).
services.public.title: Services on all interfaces
services.public.desc: Overview of services reachable from every network interface.
services.risky.title: Exposure of risky services
services.risky.desc: Databases, admin panels and legacy protocols reachable from everywhere are frequent attack targets.
services.risky.fix: Bind them to 127.0.0.1 or restrict them with a firewall; stop services that are not needed (ReviveGuard never stops services).
permissions.module.title: File permissions
sysctl.module.title: Kernel hardening
services.module.title: Services and ports
sysctl.container: Running in a container: kernel parameters belong to the host, so sysctl checks are skipped.
services.no_ss: The 'ss' tool is not available; service checks are skipped.
services.unreadable: The list of listening ports could not be read.
fix.service.sysctl_runtime: Applied to the running kernel immediately. Rollback restores the file; the running values stay until reboot.
fix.reason.sysctl_manual: routing-related settings depend on how this host is used (router, VPN, Docker); change them manually after review.
fix.reason.service_manual: ReviveGuard never stops services or changes bindings; follow the recommendation.
language.no_terminal: No terminal. Use: reviveguard config set language <code>
error.config_write: Cannot write the configuration ({detail}). Run as root or use --config.
config.usage: Usage: reviveguard config set <key> <value> | reviveguard config show
fix.service.start_fail2ban: Fail2ban will be started or reloaded (not restarted). Repeated failed logins from your own address could get it banned.
fix.result.packages_remain: Note: installed packages stay on the system and are not removed: {packages}.
wizard.intro: I will check this server and fix what can be fixed safely. You only confirm: nothing changes without your OK, and every file change can be undone with 'reviveguard rollback'.
wizard.scan_done: Found {count} problem(s): {critical} critical, {high} high, {medium} medium, {low} low.
wizard.nothing_to_do: Nothing to fix. The server looks good.
wizard.safe_none: No safe automatic fixes are pending.
wizard.safe_list: These fixes are safe to apply together:
wizard.access_intro: The next items can affect access or restart services, so each one asks separately.
wizard.report_failed: The report could not be saved (check permissions of the state directory).
wizard.done: Done. Run 'reviveguard audit' any time to re-check, or 'reviveguard report' for a full report.
fix.auto.none: No fixes are eligible for automatic application.
fix.auto.skip_disruptive: can affect access or restart services
fix.auto.skip_critical: critical severity needs 'allow_critical = true' in the policy
fix.auto.skip_high: high severity needs 'allow_high = true' in the policy
fix.auto.stopped: Stopped after a failure; the remaining fixes were not applied.
report.title: Security report
report.note: This report lists findings and changes. It intentionally has no numeric score: a single number would hide which problems matter. Secrets are redacted.
ssh.x11_forwarding.title: SSH X11 forwarding
ssh.x11_forwarding.desc: X11 forwarding exposes the client's graphical session to the server and is rarely needed on servers.
ssh.max_auth_tries.title: SSH authentication attempts limit
ssh.max_auth_tries.desc: A high limit lets one connection try many passwords or keys before it is dropped.
ssh.max_auth_tries.fix: Set 'MaxAuthTries 4' (ReviveGuard can apply this). Clients that offer many keys from an agent may need 'IdentitiesOnly yes'.
ssh.grace_time.title: SSH login grace time
ssh.grace_time.desc: A long grace time lets unauthenticated connections occupy the server for minutes.
ssh.weak_algorithms.title: Weak SSH algorithms
ssh.weak_algorithms.desc: Old ciphers, MACs and key exchanges are enabled; they are broken or weak.
ssh.weak_algorithms.fix: Remove them with '-' entries (ReviveGuard can apply this). Very old clients may stop connecting.
ssh.default_port.title: SSH port
ssh.default_port.desc: Port 22 is scanned constantly by bots; a different port removes most automated noise (it is not a security boundary by itself).
ssh.default_port.fix: Add a new port, test it, then drop 22 (ReviveGuard does this in two safe steps).
ssh.port_migration.title: SSH port migration
ssh.port_migration.desc: SSH listens on both the old port 22 and a new port; the migration is not finished.
ssh.port_migration.fix: Log in through the new port, then run 'reviveguard fix --check SSH-011' to close port 22.
fix.next.port_added: open a NEW terminal and check that 'ssh -p {port} <user>@<server>' works. Keep this session open. Then, from that new session, run 'reviveguard fix --check SSH-011' to close port 22. Open the new port in your cloud provider's firewall too, if it has one.
fix.next.port_finished: port {old} is closed. Connect with 'ssh -p {port} <user>@<server>' from now on; also update any scripts, monitoring and your provider's firewall.
fix.reason.ssh_socket: SSH is socket-activated (ssh.socket), so ports come from the socket unit; change it with 'systemctl edit ssh.socket' yourself.
fix.reason.port_in_main: sshd_config sets 'Port' itself; remove it there first or change the port manually.
fix.reason.firewall_open_port: a firewall is active and does not allow the new port {port}. Allow it first (e.g. 'ufw allow {port}/tcp'), then run this fix again.
fix.reason.reconnect_new_port: you are connected through port 22. Reconnect through the new port ('ssh -p {port} ...') and run this fix from that session; otherwise you could lose access.
fix.reason.port_not_listening: sshd is not listening on port {port} yet.
accounts.module.title: Accounts
accounts.needs_root: Password states can only be read as root.
accounts.admin_user.title: Administrator account
accounts.admin_user.desc: Only root can administer this server over SSH. A dedicated key-only administrator lets you disable direct root login and keeps an audit trail of who did what.
accounts.admin_user.fix: Run 'reviveguard admin-user' (or 'reviveguard wizard') to create one.
accounts.empty_password.title: Accounts with empty passwords
accounts.empty_password.desc: A login-capable account without a password can be used by anyone who can reach a login prompt.
accounts.empty_password.fix: Lock or set a password: 'passwd -l <user>' (ReviveGuard never changes accounts silently).
accounts.extra_root.title: Extra superuser accounts
accounts.extra_root.desc: Accounts other than root with UID 0 have full control and are a classic backdoor.
accounts.extra_root.fix: Review and remove or renumber them manually ('usermod -u').
admin.title: Administrator account
admin.intro: I will create a separate administrator with sudo and key-only login, so root login and passwords can be switched off safely afterwards.
admin.key_help: Paste your PUBLIC key: one line starting with ssh-ed25519 or ssh-rsa (on your computer: 'cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub'; no key yet? run 'ssh-keygen -t ed25519' there first).
admin.ask_key: Public key (press Enter to skip and add it later):
admin.err.bad_name: Invalid name: use lowercase letters, digits, '_' or '-' (2-31 characters, starting with a letter).
admin.err.reserved: This name is reserved by the system; choose another one.
admin.err.bad_key: This is not a valid public key line (it must be a single 'ssh-ed25519 AAAA...' style line; options such as command= are not accepted, and never paste a private key).
admin.err.exists: The account '{name}' already exists; choose another name.
admin.err.no_sudo_group: The 'sudo' group does not exist on this system.
admin.err.no_visudo: 'visudo' is not available to validate the sudoers file.
fix.access.admin_user: create the account '{name}' (home, bash, group sudo), install login key {fingerprint}, sudo: {sudo}
fix.access.user_stays: ReviveGuard never deletes users: 'reviveguard rollback' removes the files it writes, but the account stays.
fix.next.admin_user: open a NEW terminal and check that 'ssh {name}@<server>' works and 'sudo -v' succeeds. Then reconnect as {name} and run 'sudo reviveguard wizard': it will offer to switch off root login and passwords.
fix.next.admin_user_password: set its password as root: 'passwd {name}'. Then open a NEW terminal, check 'ssh {name}@<server>' and 'sudo -v'; reconnect as {name} and run 'sudo reviveguard wizard'.
fix.reason.admin_user_cmd: it needs your input (a name and a public key): run 'reviveguard admin-user'.
fix.reason.lock_account: lock the account yourself: 'passwd -l <user>', after checking that nothing depends on it.
fix.reason.extra_root: review these accounts and fix them by hand.
wizard.admin_offer: Only root can administer this server. A dedicated administrator account is the foundation for safely switching off root login and passwords.
wizard.admin_created: Account created. Test it in a new terminal, reconnect as that user and run 'sudo reviveguard wizard' again to finish the SSH hardening.
fix.firewall.enable_ufw: enable ufw with 'deny incoming' by default; allowed (they are reachable today): {allow}; stays blocked: {blocked}
fix.service.ufw_enable: This changes who can reach the server. It is applied only with your live confirmation: if you do not confirm in time, the firewall is switched off again.
fix.confirm.firewall: Open a NEW terminal NOW and check that you can still connect (allowed ports: {ports}). Then type 'ok' here.
fix.confirm.waiting: Waiting {seconds} s for 'ok' (no answer = the change is reverted)...
fix.result.confirmation_failed: No confirmation received; the change was reverted ({detail}).
fix.next.ufw_enabled: when you start a new service, allow its port ('ufw allow <port>/tcp'); check 'ufw status verbose'. Rolling back only restores the files, so use 'ufw disable' to switch it off.
fix.reason.ufw_no_ss: the listening ports could not be read ('ss' is missing), so the firewall rules cannot be derived safely.
docker.socket.title: Docker socket permissions
docker.socket.desc: Anyone who can use the Docker socket controls the whole host (root-equivalent).
docker.socket.fix: Restrict it: 'chmod 660 /var/run/docker.sock' and keep it in group docker.
docker.group.title: Members of the docker group
docker.group.desc: Members of the docker group can become root on this host; the list should be short and intentional.
docker.group.fix: Remove users that do not need Docker: 'gpasswd -d <user> docker'.
docker.api.title: Docker API exposure
docker.api.desc: An unauthenticated Docker API on a network address gives remote root to anyone who reaches it.
docker.api.fix: Remove tcp:// hosts from daemon.json or protect them with TLS client certificates and a firewall.
docker.privileged.title: Privileged containers
docker.privileged.desc: Privileged containers have almost the same access as the host.
docker.privileged.fix: Remove --privileged and grant only the capabilities needed.
docker.host_network.title: Containers on the host network
docker.host_network.desc: Host networking removes network isolation between the container and the host.
docker.host_network.fix: Use a bridge network and publish only the needed ports.
docker.capabilities.title: Containers with dangerous capabilities
docker.capabilities.desc: Capabilities such as SYS_ADMIN or ALL allow escaping the container.
docker.capabilities.fix: Drop them (--cap-drop ALL) and add back only what is required.
docker.mounts.title: Sensitive host mounts
docker.mounts.desc: Mounting /, /etc, /root or the Docker socket into a container gives it control of the host.
docker.mounts.fix: Mount only the specific directories needed, read-only where possible.
docker.root_user.title: Containers running as root
docker.root_user.desc: A process running as root inside a container is more dangerous if the container is compromised.
docker.root_user.fix: Run as an unprivileged user (USER in the Dockerfile or --user).
docker.module.title: Docker
docker.not_installed: Docker is not installed; Docker checks are skipped.
docker.needs_root: Containers can only be inspected as root.
docker.unreadable: The container list could not be read (is the Docker daemon running?).
fix.reason.docker_manual: ReviveGuard never modifies containers or restarts Docker; follow the recommendation.
fix.reason.auth_unknown: I cannot tell how this SSH session logged in (no matching entry in the SSH log). Without proof that your key works, narrowing access could lock you out; log in with your public key in a NEW terminal and run this from that session.
fix.reason.logged_in_with_password: this session logged in with '{method}', not a public key. A key in authorized_keys may not be yours, so disabling passwords or root could lock you out. Log in with your public key in a NEW terminal and run this from that session.
rollback.reloaded: The {service} service was reloaded with the restored files.
rollback.reload_failed: The files were restored but {service} could not be reloaded: do it yourself ('systemctl reload {service}').
rollback.reload_skipped: The files were restored, but the {service} configuration does not validate, so it was not reloaded. Check it with 'sshd -t'.
admin.no_key_note: No key now: the account '{name}' will be created WITHOUT a login key, so nobody can log in as '{name}' until you add one with 'reviveguard add-key --name {name}'. Root login and passwords will stay as they are.
admin.err.no_such_user: There is no suitable account named '{name}' (root cannot be used here).
fix.access.add_key: add the login key {fingerprint} to the account '{name}' (existing keys are kept)
fix.next.admin_user_nokey: the account has no login key yet, so nobody can log in as {name}. On your computer run 'cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub', then here: 'reviveguard add-key --name {name}' and paste the line. Then test 'ssh {name}@<server>' in a NEW terminal.
fix.next.key_added: open a NEW terminal and check that 'ssh {name}@<server>' works and 'sudo -v' succeeds. Then reconnect as {name} and run 'sudo reviveguard wizard' to switch off root login and passwords.
wizard.admin_failed_skip: The administrator account was not created, so I skip the steps that narrow access (root login, passwords): they could lock you out. Run 'reviveguard admin-user' and then 'reviveguard wizard' again.
fix.confirm.ssh: Open a NEW terminal NOW and log in to this server the way you normally do (with your key). Only if it works, type 'ok' here. If you cannot get in, do NOT type anything: the change will be reverted automatically.
fix.confirm.ssh_port: Open a NEW terminal NOW and log in through port {port} ('ssh -p {port} <user>@<server>'). Only if it works, type 'ok' here. Otherwise type nothing: the change will be reverted automatically.
ssh.authkeys_perms.title: authorized_keys permissions
ssh.authkeys_perms.desc: sshd (StrictModes) silently ignores keys when the file, ~/.ssh or the home directory is writable by others or owned by someone else, so key logins stop working.
ssh.authkeys_perms.fix: Fix the listed paths: 'chmod go-w <path>' and 'chown <user> <path>'.
fix.reason.authkeys_manual: permissions inside home directories are fixed by hand: follow the recommendation.
accounts.password_policy.title: Password quality policy
accounts.password_policy.desc: Without a password-quality policy users can set short, guessable passwords; this matters most when passwords are the way in.
accounts.password_policy.fix: Install libpam-pwquality and require at least 12 characters (ReviveGuard can do this; it affects new passwords only).
fix.passwords.policy: require new passwords of at least {length} characters with 3 character classes (libpam-pwquality)
fix.confirm.ssh_root: Open a NEW terminal NOW and log in as an ADMINISTRATOR, not as root ('ssh {admins}@<server>'), then check 'sudo -v'. Only if it works, type 'ok' here. Otherwise type nothing: root login will be restored automatically.
admin.password_later: Without a key and a password nobody can log in as '{name}'. Set a password later with 'passwd {name}' or add a key with 'reviveguard add-key --name {name}'.
admin.password_next: open a NEW terminal and log in as {name} with this password; 'sudo -v' asks for it. Then run 'sudo reviveguard wizard': it will offer to switch off root login (your login by password stays).
admin.password_failed: The password for '{name}' was not set. Try again with 'passwd {name}'.
